text:
sam-infra: quick heads up — found a partner ingestion S3 bucket that contains a tarball with an env dump. looks like several VAULT_ADDR and a couple of KMS-wrapped blobs. not yet sure if plaintext creds included. tagging @maria-sec and @kevin-eng for containment.

maria-sec: on it. first step: snapshot the object and lock down bucket ACLs/readers. do not delete yet. can you paste the object path? :eyes:

sam-infra: s3://partner-ingest-prod/2026-03-21/ingest-20260321-01.tar.gz. md5 matches what the partner support said. I ran `strings` locally and saw: `VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.prod.redwood.internal` and two lines of base64 blobs like `Ci0tLS1CRUdJTiBLSV...` which look like KMS ciphertext.

maria-sec: good. containment checklist: 1) restrict bucket to partner support + platform-admins 2) rotate any SA keys that could be in that env 3) pivot Vault unseal tokens if present 4) enable longer audit retention for this object path. jordan-sre, can you apply the ACL lockdown?
jordan-sre: applying now. running: `aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket partner-ingest-prod --policy file://lockdown.json` — will add org-only allow and remove public/partner role. ping when done.

incidents-bot: Ticket INC-2026-042 created by maria-sec: "Partner ingest bucket contains potential env leak; containment in progress" assigned to @maria-sec, priority P1.

kevin-eng: quick vuln triage note: KMS-wrapped blobs likely mean partners encrypted secrets with our KMS key (or theirs) before sending. If it's our KMS-ciphertext, compromise scope is high (service tokens may be recoverable). Need to check which key resource id is on the ciphertext header. sam, can you pull the first 2 lines of the ciphertext header?
sam-infra: header: `projects/rdw-prod/locations/global/keyRings/ingest/cryptoKeys/ingest-wrapping-key` — looks like our key.
maria-sec: that's bad. assume decryption possible. Next steps: 1) generate list of SA/service tokens that had access to that key in last 30d 2) rotate those SA keys / revoke tokens 3) rotate any Vault wrapping keys and rewrap all ciphertext we control. kevin, can you draft the rotation plan?

kevin-eng: drafting now. high-level: - immediate: remove IAM bindings on `projects/rdw-prod/.../ingest-wrapping-key` for non-essential principals; add temporary deny for partner-accounts. - revoke long-lived SA keys that appear in access logs (gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable/delete). - rotate Vault transit keys: run `vault write -f transit/keys/ingest-wrapping-key/rotate` and rewrap existing ciphertexts used by our pipelines. - longer: audit logs backfill and engagement with partner to get plaintext origin. Will post commands.

kevin-eng: command snippets: ```
# list recent principals that used the key
gcloud logging read "resource.type=key_ring AND protoPayload.methodName:projects.cryptoKeys.decrypt" --freshness=30d --format="json(payload)" | jq -r '.[].protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail' | sort | uniq

# disable SA keys
gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=svc-ingest@rdw-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --format=json | jq -r '.[].name' | xargs -n1 gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable --key

# rotate vault transit key
vault write -f transit/keys/ingest-wrapping-key/rotate
```

maria-sec: also enable full audit logging on the KMS key and export to a locked GCS bucket for retention. add a watch rule for any decrypt calls. harper-pm, do we need a customer notification?
harper-pm: yes — customer-impact TBD. Notify partner legal and security teams; we'll decide external disclosure after initial scope confirmed. I'll draft a short statement.

jordan-sre: ACL change applied. policy id 9f2a... removed partner role from bucket. confirmed no public ACLs. snapshot saved to gs://forensics/partner-ingest/1809991234/ingest-20260321-01.tar.gz

sam-infra: copied the header metadata and uploaded to the ticket. also ran `openssl asn1parse` on the ciphertext and confirmed the key resource string is present.

maria-sec: make sure we also rotate any Vault wrapped-wrapping-keys (transit keys used to wrap unseal tokens). run an emergency rewrap for all active ciphertexts created in last 90d with that key. kevin, can you coordinate with ops to throttle rewrap so it doesn't blow up traffic?

kevin-eng: yes. plan: create a canary rewrap job for a small prefix, measure latency, then bulk rewrap with batching. use the built-in rewrap endpoint: `POST /internal/rewrap` (internal only) with rate limit 100/s.

kevin-eng: example rewrap job config: ```json
{"prefix":"ingest/2026/","batch_size":200,"concurrency":4}
```

maria-sec: RBAC changes: after rotation we should lock down `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` to just platform-kms-proxy and key-owners group. open a policy PR and request 2 approvals.

sam-infra: found one plaintext API key in the tarball (looks like a partner service token) — not ours but we should still ask partner to rotate. I redacted a copy and pushed to forensics.

incidents-bot: Update INC-2026-042: jordan-sre added snapshot artifacts; kevin-eng added rotation plan draft.

maria-sec: ops task list for next 6 hours: - restrict KMS access (kevin) - revoke suspicious SA keys (kevin) - rewrap traffic canary (kevin + jordan) - enable audit export + retention (jordan) - contact partner and legal (harper). Please mark done as you complete.

kevin-eng: starting IAM deny now. disabling two SA keys that show decrypt calls. will post command output when done. :white_check_mark:

sam-infra: quick note on detection: adding a regex to our partner-ingest pipeline to reject tarballs containing VAULT_ADDR or `VAULT_TOKEN` plaintext. patching in PR #4821.

maria-sec: great. also add an alert rule to redirect any future uploads containing base64 blocks > 300 chars to security-review queue.

harper-pm: draft customer email ready for review, will post in the ticket.

kevin-eng: SA key disable outputs: `disabled key: projects/rdw-prod/serviceAccounts/svc-ingest@rdw-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com/keys/ABCD1234`. revoked long-lived key and created a short-lived Workload Identity binding.

maria-sec: OK. once rewrap canary passes, proceed with bulk. keep audit exports immutable. after rotation, schedule an RBAC enforcement window to remove any unnecessary grants across project boundaries.

sam-infra: can confirm canary rewrap succeeded for 3k objects, no downstream failures in pipelines. monitoring for 30m.

jordan-sre: audit export enabled to gs://secure-audit-exports/ingest/1809991234 with retention 365d and CMEK. alerts wired.

maria-sec: closing interim incident state. follow-ups: postmortem, policy PR for stricter KMS RBAC, partner engagement report, and automation to reject secrets in uploads. thanks all. :pray:

harper-pm: noted. I'll schedule a postmortem meeting tomorrow and add action owners.

sam-infra: any other blockers?

kevin-eng: none from my side. moving ticket to monitoring.

maria-sec: thanks team. leaving this thread open until postmortem artifacts are published.
